issues.description: Field naming mismatch in ExcellenceLand: the UML/problem statement defines a boolean attribute named 'excellentEnough' (problem_statement.md declares '-excellentEnough: boolean'), but the solution implementation declares a boolean field named 'isExcellent' with a getter isExcellent(). This identifier mismatch between the specification (which students should follow) and the provided solution can confuse students about the exact attribute name and expected public getter, and may cause automated tests that expect 'excellentEnough' or an isExcellentEnough()/getExcellentEnough() getter to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the UML/problem statement: in ExcellenceLand, rename the boolean field to 'excellentEnough' (private boolean excellentEnough;) and provide the corresponding public getter (preferably boolean isExcellentEnough()). Update the public constructor parameter name to 'excellentEnough' and assign it to the field. Ensure any tests or references use the 'excellentEnough' field/getter name so students implement the attribute exactly as specified.

issues.description: Boolean attribute mismatch for ExcellenceLand: the UML in problem_statement.md declares a boolean attribute named 'excellentEnough' (problem_statement.md line 36). The solution implementation declares the corresponding field as 'isExcellent' with getter isExcellent() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java line 8). The template file for ExcellenceLand is empty (template_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java lines 1-3). Because the exercise requires students to implement attributes and public getters exactly as in the UML, this difference (excellentEnough vs isExcellent) creates ambiguity about the expected attribute identifier and getter name (students might expect isExcellentEnough()/getExcellentEnough() based on the UML but find isExcellent() in the provided solution/reference).
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent identifier and apply it across artifacts. Two clear options: (A) Rename the solution field and getter to match the UML: private boolean excellentEnough; public boolean isExcellentEnough() (or public boolean getExcellentEnough()), and update the constructor parameter name to 'excellentEnough' in the same parameter order. Or (B) Update the UML/problem statement to declare the boolean as 'isExcellent' (and document the getter as isExcellent()). Ensure constructor parameter names/order and the public getter name are updated accordingly so the UML, template, and solution use the same identifier.
